slot.brief: Given limiting molar conductivities of some strong electrolytes, construct Λ° of a weak electrolyte (e.g., CH3COOH or a sparingly soluble salt) by linear combination — moderate numerical.

stem: At $25^\circ\text{C}$, $\Lambda_m^\circ$ values for $\text{HCl}$, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ are $426$, $126$ and $91\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, respectively. Find $\Lambda_m^\circ$ for $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

verdicts.working: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426 + 91 − 126 = 391 S cm² mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})$ $=426+91-126=391\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.
